title: A solid is rigid and keeps a definite shape
summary: A solid is rigid and keeps a definite shape, and its volume hardly changes when the pressure changes.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says a solid is rigid and possesses a definite shape. The same section says both solid and liquid samples have volumes that are very nearly independent of pressure. A liquid, which flows and takes the container's shape, is a different card, and so is a gas, which takes the container's volume as well. Sand can be poured, but the page says that happens because sand is many small solid grains, not because a solid loses its shape. The page does not rank materials from soft to hard. Hardness is named elsewhere as a physical property, not measured here.

sources.note: OpenStax Chemistry, first-edition path /books/chemistry/, CC BY 4.0. Supports the rigid solid of definite shape, and the note that sand pours because it is many small solid grains, in section 1.2. Paraphrase only; the section was not copied.
